Title: ​Health action schools - Another step forward

NewsContent:
"​The Health Action Schools (HAS) team of the Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED) conducted a three-day workshop for teachers on health promotion in schools. The workshop led by Dr Tashmin Khamis, Assistant Professor, AKU-IED, in partnership with Save the Children Fund and facilitated by Mr Hugh Hawes, founder of the Child-to-Child Trust, held its final session on Friday, February 12. Over thirty teachers from government and private schools attended the workshop.

The HAS pilot project aims to establish schools, which integrate health education with the school environment and health services. The sessions focused on active learning by children, easy-to-use. inexpensive resources, life-skills and health action integrating health education and lesson planning. Special attention was given to storytelling, planning surveys with children, games and drama, as effective techniques to promote health education in schools in Pakistan.

Mr Hugh Hawes was born in Pakistan and is presently the Emeritus Reader at the University Of London Institute Of Education. The Child-to-Child movement, which he co-founded with David Morley, is actively involved in 80 countries to enable children to become health promoters in their communities and school settings.

Established in ] 993, as the Aga Khan University's first programme outside the health sciences, AKU-IED is dedicated to the professional development of teachers and overall school improvement in Pakistan and other developing countries. The Institute is committed to leading reform and fostering leadership in education through innovation, practice, policy development and outreach initiatives."
